items.criterion: FAILIF: GETTING-STARTED.md still claims a generated/ sibling of the spec directory, or grep -cin mcp returns fewer than 3, or the documented mcp start protocol disagrees with the real flags. PROOF: the greps and the mcp start --help output plus a real health probe.
items.detail: All three disjuncts checked and none fires. (a) Sibling claim: `grep -in sibling GETTING-STARTED.md` => exit 1, no match. GETTING-STARTED.md:56-61 states the rule `<directory containing the spec>/../generated/` with two measured cases; line 61 (`specs/foo.spec.md` -> `<project root>/generated/foo/function.ts`) is that same rule applied (specDir=`specs`, `..`=root), not a sibling-of-the-spec-directory claim. Code agrees: src/cascade/index.ts:85-86 `const specDir = path.dirname(specPath); const generatedDir = path.join(specDir, '..', 'generated');` and src/cascade/index.ts:396,411 `fileName = block.name.replace(/-/g,'_')+'.ts'` joined onto outputDir, so block `hello/function` -> `specs/generated/hello/function.ts`. Artifact on disk confirms: specs/generated/hello/function.ts header reads `Source: @speclang/examples/hello-world#hello/function`. (b) `grep -cin mcp GETTING-STARTED.md` => 15 (>=3). (c) Flags: `node bin/speclang mcp start --help` exit 0 prints `-p, --port <port> ... (default: "3000")`, `-d, --dir <directory> ... (default: ".")`, `--remote`, `--auth <type> ... (default: "none")`, `--user`, `--pass`, `--token`, `--config` — GETTING-STARTED.md:79-88 documents exactly these (omitting `--config` is an omission, not a disagreement). Real probe: `node bin/speclang mcp start --remote --port 3917` then `curl -s localhost:3917/health` => `{"status":"ok","mode":"http"}` (doc:96,104); `POST /mcp/message tools/list` => `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"tools":[{"name":"speclang_search",...}]},"id":1}` (doc:108); `tools/call speclang_cascade_status` => `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"status":"idle"},"id":2}` (doc:113); `GET /mcp` => `event: endpoint` / `data: /mcp/message?sessionId=8420b3ee-...` (doc:94). Startup diagnostics observed on stderr only (/tmp/mcp_err.log), stdout empty, matching doc:116-117. The mcp.pid caveat at doc:117-118 is true: bin/speclang:1420 and :1459 read `.speclang/mcp.pid`, while `mcp start` (bin/speclang:1353-1412) never writes it. Tests: `npx vitest run tests/mcp tests/cli` => exit 0, `Test Files 17 passed (17)`, `Tests 200 passed | 2 skipped (202)`. [resolution 0.04; GETTING-STARTED.md]
